p: in which is the life of all."
It is the custom of Yisrael to say,
on the Shabbos when Rosh Chodesh is blessed,
that You grant us long life,
is inclusive, corresponding to the ten Sefiros.
And we put long life first,
is "for the world that is entirely long"
for length even of several thousand years,
And Shabbos is a semblance of the World to Come;
which is the Long One, Atik.
we ask for every kind of life;
as is said in the holy Zohar
"All the life of the world that they inherit
depends on this World to Come,
for it is the life of all,
מִי הָאִישׁ הֶחָפֵץ חַיִּים וְגוֹ׳ (תְּהִלִּים לד, יג-טו)
'Who is the man who desires life,' etc. (Tehillim 34:13-15),
'He who guards his mouth and his tongue.'"
It brings this pasuk from Mishlei
וּכְתִיב מִי הָאִישׁ הֶחָפֵץ חַיִּים כוּ׳
And it is written, "Who is the man who desires life," etc.:
that is called the World to Come," etc.;
"this is the Name of the Holy King,
which is bound to those supernal days
that are called 'the days of the heavens upon the earth';
the days of the heavens, certainly;
of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah.
is the Holy One, blessed be He,
is what the holy Zohar calls
and it is sun and moon;
and that is why it says "certainly."
when the moon receives from the sun
from the Holy One, blessed be He,
Who is "a sun and a shield,"
"So that your days may be multiplied," etc.,
"as the days of the heavens upon the earth"
"Who is the man who desires life":
"as the days of the heavens, certainly,
for the moon then receives from the sun,
and we ask it on Shabbos,
And the Shabbos before Rosh Chodesh
includes the holiness of the coming month,
for Shabbos is the sum of all the days

for if one wishes to sanctify the tongue,
from foods that are not in holiness.
the holy Zohar brings the pasuk

the main intent is guarding the tongue,
for the one depends on the other.
וְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א לב, א)

and since Shabbos is called speech," etc.
And in Sefer Yetzirah it is stated
is the mouth in the soul;
He explains "mouth" as eating in holiness,
for on Shabbos a person's eating is in holiness;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם מז, ב)
as is said in the holy Zohar (there, 47b):
this is the Oral Torah," etc.
And this is what it says,
"a different, supernal place is so called"
And this is that the one depends on the other,
along the lines of what Tosafos write
in the name of the Midrash:
that delicacies not enter his body."
בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק כו)
in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu (Eliyahu Rabbah ch. 26).
And the essence of life is the words of Torah,
"See, I have set before you today
And this is the matter of what is said in the Mechilta
only to those who ate the manna,
and second to them, those who eat terumah."
And if the plain meaning were
because their heart is free for Torah
and they are not occupied with their livelihood
after all, there were those such as
Rabbi Elazar ben Charsom and the like,
וְגַם לָמָּה לֹא זָכְרוּ אוֹכְלֵי מַעֲשֵׂר
And also, why did they not mention those who eat maaser?
For the Levi'im were one tribe of twelve,
and they were given one part in ten
and they were free for Torah.
But the intent is as we said:
that the eating be in holiness.
Therefore they mentioned those who ate the manna,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב סא, ב)
as is said in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 61b),
that it enters the soul more than anything
and is separated more from the body, etc.;
second to them, those who eat terumah,

like the service of the Beis HaMikdash."
that words of Torah will be absorbed into one's heart.

that the one depends on the other,

which has two signs of purity:
וְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה יג, ה)

for it praises the Holy One, blessed be He," etc.;
"'and the hyrax' — this is Madai," etc.,
"for it praises the Holy One, blessed be He";
for it praises the Holy One, blessed be He," etc.
And this is that for this
the sign of purity in eating indicates
that it praises the Holy One, blessed be He.
'and it does not chew the cud'

for it did not praise the Holy One, blessed be He,
אַנְתְּ רֵישָׁא דִּי דַהֲבָא (דָּנִיֵּאל ב, לח)
"I will ascend above the heights of the clouds,
I will be like the Most High";
and Paras and Madai correspond to desire,
and envy and anger correspond to Yavan,
כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
is as if he worships idols";
and the end of pride is idolatry,
"I will ascend above the heights of the clouds,
I will be like the Most High";
is the root of all the kelipos,
and it corresponds to the lying tongue;
here is the falsehood that I created in My world."
And it corresponds to lashon hara,
עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים
'a tongue that speaks great things,'" etc.
וְהוּא יֵשׁ לוֹ סִימַן טָהֳרָה הַנִּגְלֶה
And it has the revealed sign of purity,
"for he had game in his mouth" (Bereishis 25:28);
when the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts payment from Esav,
He wraps himself in his tallis like an elder
וּבָא וְיוֹשֵׁב לוֹ אֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב וְכוּלֵּי
and comes and sits beside Yaakov," etc.
אַךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹמֵר (עוֹבַדְיָה א, ד)
"Though you set your nest among the stars,
from there I will bring you down, says Hashem."
And it is written after it (there, 6):
For Hashem Yisbarach reveals the depth of his heart,
"and seven abominations are in his heart" (Mishlei 26:25).
have the internal sign of purity,
and about this they said in the Midrash Rabbah
that it praises the Holy One, blessed be He;
they have the sign of impurity.
And the verse varied its wording,
for regarding the camel it is written,
"but it does not split the hoof,"
"but it will not split the hoof,"
"but it did not split the hoof,"
the camel, which alludes to the kingdom of Bavel,
in it the evil is explicit in the revealed things,
which alludes to the kingdom of Paras
and about them it is stated (Berachos 8b):
"and they are modest in intimate matters";
"From the disgrace of that wicked one
וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נִקְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים
and for this Yisrael are called holy
"but it will not split the hoof,"
for its vileness is destined to be revealed;
and begin with words of Torah," etc.;
for when the wine went in,
there came out from the depths of his heart,
and he wanted them to do a thing
even for the dissolute of the nations of the world,
as she sent back to him,
and this is "but it will not split the hoof,"
which alludes to the kingdom of Yavan,
as is expounded in the Pesikta
for the Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing against them
which they received from their fathers;
this is the kingdom of Yavan," etc.

this is the kingdom of Yavan,
"because there is among all the kingdoms
none that come close to the way of faith
established a straight path in character traits,
what is fitting in this world for conduct,
so that the early authorities cited
in their books from the words of their wise men.
But at the root of their wisdom
and they wrote that it was afterward found
that he was full of lusts and abominations.

"but it did not split the hoof":
for at the root it has the impurity
in the sign of the revealed things.
when the eating is in holiness,
